             # # Report generation              # # Key functions: Generating reports based on meta-data              save_ms5rawlevels =TRUE,              visualreport=FALSE,              dofirstpage = TRUE,              viewingwindow=1)

Best regards,

Evelyn

Thanks Marcus and Vincent,

Apart from Vincent's input, I think you still have an issue with the time resolution. Defining qwindow as decimal numbers when you need a high precision in the minutes bring this problem.

For example, using your method and converting back the data to timestamps, you can see we don't get exactly the timestamps we expect:

library(lubridate)

seg_timestamp <-  c(
  "07:00", "08:00", "08:55", "09:50",
  "10:10", "11:05", "12:00", "12:30",
  "13:00", "13:30", "14:25", "15:20",
  "15:40", "16:35", "17:30", "18:30",
  "23:00")

seg_hours = period_to_seconds(hm(seg_timestamp))/3600
print(seg_hours)
back_conversion = seconds_to_period(seg_hours*3600)
print(back_conversion)
[1] "7H 0M 0S" "8H 0M 0S" [3] "8H 54M 59.9999999999964S" "9H 50M 0S" [5] "10H 10M 0S" "11H 5M 0S" [7] "12H 0M 0S" "12H 30M 0S" [9] "13H 0M 0S" "13H 30M 0S" [11] "14H 25M 0S" "15H 20M 0S" [13] "15H 40M 0S" "16H 34M 59.9999999999927S" [15] "17H 30M 0S" "18H 30M 0S" [17] "23H 0M 0S"

The reason it works in part 2 is that there we already implemented a check in the past a check for the time resolution and we use the closest epoch in the case that the resolution between epoch length and qwindow does not match. However I think this is not implemented in part 5 yet as this functionality is way more recent.

ID04        07:00:00    08:00:00    08:55:00    09:50:00    10:10:00    11:05:00
.....

Jairo

To do this, I am trying to process my accelerometery data (approximately 10 minutes of data captured) using GGIR. However, GGIR doesn't seem to like the small file size i am using.

Is there a way I can get around this?

Also, is there a way to get which 'intensity zone' the participant was in according to time?

Best wishes,

Karl

Hi Mark,

The glossary is based on https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#4_Inspecting_the_results which provides the template. From there you need to take into account your custom script parameters. Feel free to send me the name of a specific variable and I'll decipher it for you to say what the value should represent.

You can calculate MVPA by specifying decimals of an hour e.g. 09:15 to 10:05 for a time in the school day could would be qwindow = c(9.25,10.0833) and you can run a script per school if you have them separated that way.
Alternatively there is the functionality to read in custom times for each individual which I think is available in the public release of GGIR now (Myself, Alex and others in our group paid for this functionality to be incorporated in GGIR with a grant). For this you need to make a .csv and call it in the script instead of the qwindow (qwindow = "C:/data/custom qwindows file.csv"). See attached a basic example. you can then put the ID's on the left with their specific school starting times with dates in the columns. This then gives you summary variables for those segments like the way you were already specifying qwindow previously. Please le me know if that covers your needs?

Thanks,
Ben

Dear Karl,

Sorry for the wait. I am not sure whether this works but I would try specifying:
windowsizes = c(5, 60, 60)  # tells GGIR to only use show epochs/window.
minimumFileSizeMB = 0 (or if that crashes, maybe 0.1 or 1)
do.cal = FALSE # turns off autocalibration
see argument documentation for backup.cal.coef to load and use calibration coefficients for your recording derived in a different recording.
mode = 1 # only run GGIR part 1 because there is no point in trying to do the rest
I would not recommend working with ENMO for this kind of experiments as you cannot guarantee good calibration. Metrics like HFEN or MAD are probably easier toj justify.
Next run GGIR and load the content of the resulting milestone data from the meta/basic output folder with the load() function in R. This then gives you object M$metashort with the epoch level values of the acceleration metrics.

The alternative approach is to replace GGIR by loading the raw data with GGIRread::readGENEactiv() and then writing your own code for calculating the acceleration metrics. In that way you are also more in control of which time segment of the treadmill experiment you use for the epochs. GGIR simply takes epochs relative to the minute.

Good luck, this is my free advise if you want me to help write scripts then that would have to go via paid consultancy.

Vincent
